problem_text: Find the largest possible integer k, such that the following statement is true: Let 2009 arbitrary non-degenerated triangles be given. In every triangle the three sides are coloured, such that one is blue, one is red and one is white. Now, for every colour separately, let us sort the lengths of the sides. We obtain b_1 <= b_2 <= ... <= b_{2009} (blue), r_1 <= r_2 <= ... <= r_{2009} (red), and w_1 <= w_2 <= ... <= w_{2009} (white). Then there exist k indices j such that we can form a non-degenerated triangle with side lengths b_j, r_j, w_j.
solution_text: The answer is 1. Proof: (1) k >= 1: Consider the largest side among all 6027 sides. WLOG say it is w_{2009}. This side came from some triangle T with sides (b, r, w_{2009}) where b and r are the blue and red sides of T. By the triangle inequality in T, b + r > w_{2009}. Since b_{2009} is the largest blue side, b_{2009} >= b. Similarly r_{2009} >= r. Therefore b_{2009} + r_{2009} >= b + r > w_{2009}. Since w_{2009} is the largest of all sides, w_{2009} >= b_{2009} and w_{2009} >= r_{2009}, so r_{2009} + w_{2009} > b_{2009} and b_{2009} + w_{2009} > r_{2009} automatically. Thus (b_{2009}, r_{2009}, w_{2009}) forms a non-degenerate triangle. (2) k <= 1: Construct 2008 triangles with sides (epsilon, epsilon, 1) where epsilon is very small, coloring the side of length 1 as white and the two epsilon sides as blue and red. Construct 1 equilateral triangle with sides (1, 1, 1). After sorting: b_1=...=b_{2008}=epsilon, b_{2009}=1; r_1=...=r_{2008}=epsilon, r_{2009}=1; w_1=...=w_{2009}=1. For j <= 2008: b_j + r_j = 2*epsilon < 1 = w_j, so triangle inequality fails. For j = 2009: all triangle inequalities hold. Only one index works, so k = 1.
solution_summary: Use the extremal principle: the largest side overall came from a valid triangle, and the largest blue and red sides are at least as large as that triangle's blue and red sides, guaranteeing the triangle inequality. A counterexample with 2008 flat triangles and 1 equilateral triangle shows k=1 is tight.
